pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae Ia q.55 a.1
pairs.question: Utrum angeli cognoscant omnia per suam substantiam, vel per aliquas species?
pairs.answer: Et ideo solus Deus cognoscit omnia per suam essentiam. Angelus autem per suam essentiam non potest omnia cognoscere; sed oportet intellectum eius aliquibus speciebus perfici ad res cognoscendas.
pairs.derivation: Question is the first of the three posed in the prologue ("Et circa hoc quaeruntur tria. Primo: utrum..."), a genuine disjunctive utrum-question the author sets himself; capitalized first word and added terminal ?. The answer is in the article's Respondeo, but its opening ("Respondeo dicendum quod illud quo intellectus intelligit... ad res cognoscendas") is a long preamble of argument that does not yet answer; I advanced the start past it to the operative concluding sentences ("Et ideo solus Deus... ad res cognoscendas"), which are the last two sentences of the Respondeo and the actual determination. Dropped the framing "Respondeo dicendum quod"; the span is contiguous to the end of the Respondeo (next is the article title ARTICULUS 2).

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae Ia q.55 a.2
pairs.question: Utrum per species connaturales, vel species a rebus acceptas?
pairs.answer: Species per quas angeli intelligunt, non sunt a rebus acceptae, sed eis connaturales.
pairs.derivation: Question is the second posed in the prologue ("Secundo: si per species, utrum per species connaturales, vel species a rebus acceptas"); I quote only the utrum-clause as the self-contained interrogative, with first word capitalized and added ?. The answer is the operative first sentence of the article's Respondeo, which directly answers it; dropped the framing "Respondeo dicendum quod" and capitalized Species. Stopped at the first full stop; what follows ("Sic enim oportet intelligere...") begins the supporting argument.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae Ia q.55 a.3
pairs.question: Utrum angeli superiores cognoscant per species magis universales, quam inferiores?
pairs.answer: Quanto angelus fuerit superior, tanto per pauciores species universitatem intelligibilium apprehendere poterit. Et ideo oportet quod eius formae sint universaliores, quasi ad plura se extendentes unaquaeque earum.
pairs.derivation: Question is the third posed in the prologue ("Tertio: utrum angeli superiores cognoscant per species magis universales, quam inferiores"), capitalized and with added ?. The Respondeo opens with a preamble about why some things are higher ("ex hoc sunt in rebus aliqua superiora... fuerit intellectus inferior") that does not yet answer; I advanced the start to the operative answering sentences ("Sic igitur quanto angelus fuerit superior..."), dropping the leading connective "Sic igitur" and capitalizing Quanto. Span ends at "...unaquaeque earum."; what follows ("Et de hoc exemplum aliqualiter in nobis perspici potest...") is illustration.
